title: Meter Shop Rule: Member-Requested Meter Tests on Electric Service by Rate Schedule Accounts
content:
**Right to a test.** A member may ask for a meter test on an Electric Service by Rate Schedule account at any time.

**Test fee.** When the number of meter tests on the same service account requested in the 365 days ending on the day before the request date of the test being requested is below the schedule's free test allowance, the test is free. Otherwise the schedule's meter test fee is charged, but only when the meter is found within the schedule's accuracy tolerance.

**Meter found fast — refund clause no longer in force.** The former clause under which a meter found fast beyond tolerance was replaced and the member credited the energy charges of the rebill window multiplied by the error percent divided by one hundred plus the error percent is **no longer in force**; it is superseded by the current meter error refund basis.

**Meter found slow.** A meter found slow beyond tolerance is replaced; the under-registration is back-billed over the same rebill window only where the schedule permits slow-meter back-billing.

**Limit.** No more than the schedule's maximum number of billing periods is ever corrected after a meter is found outside tolerance.

### Fee outcomes (hypothetical tests, free allowance of 1)

| Tests requested in the prior 365 days | Result of this test | Test fee |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Any | None — free test |
| 1 | Within tolerance | Schedule's meter test fee |
| 1 | Fast beyond tolerance | None |
| 1 | Slow beyond tolerance | None |

### Slow meter back-billing

| Schedule | Slow meter back-billed |
|---|---|
| Schedules R, RS and FH | No |
| Schedules GS-1, GS-3, IR and LP | Yes, over the rebill window, never more than the maximum number of billing periods |

superseded_clauses: A meter found fast beyond tolerance is replaced and the member is credited, with credit_reason meter_error_refund, the overbilled share of the energy charges of the rebill window (service_msr_rebill_window_energy), which is that sum multiplied by the error percent divided by one hundred plus the error percent, rounded to the cent.
